name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
description: The same person signed in from two different places in a short amount of time — faster than someone could realistically travel between them. This usually means someone besides the real owner has their password.
ruleTitles: Impossible travel between sign-ins
Sign-in using a legacy authentication protocol
Remote PowerShell access enabled for a mailbox user

name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
description: Someone signed in to this account through a service that hides where they are really connecting from. Attackers commonly use this trick to hide their real location when they are using a stolen password.
ruleTitles: Sign-in through a known anonymiser or proxy

name: Account Manipulation
description: An account was set up so its password never has to be changed. This removes a normal safety net — if that password were ever stolen, it would keep working indefinitely.
ruleTitles: Account password set to never expire
SharePoint site permission level changed

name: Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Credentials
description: A new app was registered with the company's Microsoft 365 account. This is a normal step for connecting new business tools, but it is also the first step someone would take before giving an app broad access to company data.
ruleTitles: New application registration created
Credential added to an application's service principal

name: Account Manipulation: Additional Email Delegate Permissions
description: One person was given permission to fully open and read someone else's mailbox. This is sometimes needed for a real business reason, like covering for an assistant, but it should match something the company actually asked for.
ruleTitles: Full access permission granted on another mailbox

name: Account Manipulation: Additional Cloud Roles
description: An administrator approved an outside app's access for everyone in the company at once, rather than just for themselves. If this was not planned, it is worth checking what that app can now see or do.
ruleTitles: Tenant-wide admin consent granted to an application
High-privilege permission granted to a user-assigned application
Privileged directory role assignment
Member added to a privileged group
External guest granted access to a SharePoint site
Site collection administrator added

name: Account Manipulation: Device Registration
description: A new device was registered to the company's Microsoft 365 account. Attackers sometimes register their own device so it is trusted, which lets them keep signing in without extra checks.
ruleTitles: New device registered to Azure AD
New mobile device linked to a mailbox

name: Brute Force: Password Spraying
description: One computer tried signing in to several different accounts and failed, all within a few minutes. This is a common way attackers try to guess passwords across many accounts at once, instead of guessing many passwords against just one account.
ruleTitles: Password spray against multiple accounts from one source

name: Email Collection
description: A new route was set up for how email flows into the company. A connector added without IT's knowledge could be used to secretly redirect or copy company email.
ruleTitles: Inbound or outbound mail connector added
Mailbox content exported to a local file

name: Email Collection: Remote Email Collection
description: An unusually large number of emails were opened or copied from one mailbox in a short time. This can happen when someone has broken into the account and is copying out its contents.
ruleTitles: Mass mailbox item access within a short window

name: Email Collection: Email Forwarding Rule
description: A rule was set up on this mailbox that automatically sends a copy of incoming email to an outside address, often without the owner knowing. This is a common way attackers quietly read someone's email after breaking into their account.
ruleTitles: New inbox forwarding rule to an external address
Mail flow rule created to forward mail externally

name: Create Account: Cloud Account
description: An outside guest account, not one of the company's own employees, was given admin-level access. This is unusual and worth checking, since guest accounts are not normally given this level of control.
ruleTitles: Guest account added to a privileged directory role

name: Data from Information Repositories
description: A company-wide search was created that can look through many people's mailboxes and files at once. This tool is normally used by legal or compliance teams, but someone with admin access could misuse it to find sensitive information.
ruleTitles: eDiscovery content search created

name: Domain or Tenant Policy Modification: Trust Modification
description: The company changed how one of its email domains proves who its users are when they sign in. This is a sensitive, rarely-changed setting — someone who changes it without permission could make Microsoft trust sign-ins they control.
ruleTitles: Domain federation settings changed
Trusted network location added to sign-in policy

name: Steal Application Access Token
description: A connected app was given a powerful level of access to company data. If IT did not set this up on purpose, it is worth checking exactly what that app can now see or change.
ruleTitles: High-privilege permission granted to an application
OAuth consent grant to an unverified application

name: Data from Cloud Storage
description: One person downloaded or deleted an unusually large number of files in a short time. This can happen when an account has been taken over and someone is copying or destroying company files.
ruleTitles: Mass file download or deletion within a short window

name: Modify Authentication Process: Multi-Factor Authentication
description: Someone added a new way to prove their identity on this account (like a new phone number or app) outside of normal office hours. Attackers often do this right after stealing a password, so they can get back in even if the real owner changes it.
ruleTitles: MFA method registration outside business hours
Multi-factor authentication disabled for a user

name: Hide Artifacts: Email Hiding Rules
description: A rule was created on this mailbox that automatically marks certain incoming emails as already read. Attackers use this to hide warning emails, like security alerts, from the real owner of the account.
ruleTitles: Inbox rule created to hide incoming messages

name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
description: A link was created that lets anyone who has it open a company file, without needing to sign in. This is convenient for sharing, but it means the file is no longer limited to people inside the company.
ruleTitles: Anonymous sharing link created for a file

name: Multi-Factor Authentication Request Generation
description: One account received an unusual number of sign-in approval requests in a short time that were all turned down. Attackers sometimes send a flood of these requests, hoping the real owner will approve one by accident.
ruleTitles: Repeated MFA prompt failures for one account

name: Disable or Modify Tools
description: A sign-in security rule for the company was turned off. These rules usually block risky sign-ins, so turning one off can open a door for an attacker.
ruleTitles: Conditional access policy disabled
Data loss prevention policy disabled
Safe attachments protection disabled

name: Disable or Modify Tools: Disable or Modify Cloud Log
description: A specific account or app was excused from having its mailbox activity recorded. This is sometimes used for trusted internal tools, but it can also let someone's actions go unrecorded on purpose.
ruleTitles: Mailbox audit bypass enabled for an account
Mailbox audit logging disabled
Tenant-wide unified audit logging disabled
